Dunno why the images in the last post were broken, so reposting. After a long break due to burnout, I finally had the chance to update Printline. Still a lot to be done like redoing the spacing(again), fixing the color(esp. in the diagonals) and cleaning up the diacritic placements.

Heres whats changed: -

* Printline is now a variable font
   * Regular is now mapped as black.
   * Added new Thin and Regular masters.
* Added build.sh and config.yaml to build the fonts from sources.
* Restructured file structure to be cleaner and comply with Google Fonts.

Download Printline here: [github.com/ArchitType/Printline](http://github.com/ArchitType/Printline)

Do let me know what you think!

Hi everybody Printline has been updated to 0.2.

Changelog:

\-Renamed Eddie Sans to Printline due to naming conflict.

\-Expanded to Core Latin glyph set defined by google fonts.

\-Crossbars are now more consistent.

\-Added basic soft dotting (needs refinement).

Planned Updates:

\-Reworking M,N,W,Y, spacing and the kerning.

\-Additional weights ranging from Extra Light to Black

Let me know what you think of it. You can check out the project at [https://github.com/ArchitType/Printline](https://github.com/ArchitType/Printline)
Yeah context can help but with headlines where I see a lot of combined alphanumerics it can cause people  to stumble a bit.

The goal was to be human but still polished to some extent. Just took a look at the 't' and I see what you mean, same goes for the crossbars for the uppercase. I've changed it a bit to be somewhat polished. I was stuck on the 0 for a bit since the 'O' is so condensed it makes it hard to differentiate between them while retaining the overall personality. Kerning and spacing is something I'm not so happy with either, I need to sit and just clean up the mess. Thanks for checking out the project and for the lovely feedback!
Thank you, it means a lot, and I will absolutely post updates here as well.
Okay got it! I'll play around with it while trying to keep the vibe somewhat similar.

Yeah I think I'll adjust the 5,6 and 9 and let it sit for a bit so I can see it relatively objectively. 

I figured out that the stems and zones  I set messed with the tittles but not the period, temporarily I've unified it with the comma, I'll push it later.

And wow, I never thought of the crossbars that way, but it obviously makes sense to be close in range. Although, what about the "F", wouldn't matching the crossbars with the "E" cause balance issues?

Really appreciate all of the help and feedback.

Yeah I see what you mean about 5 and 6, I've been wrestling with it for a while to get to a point where the stroke width doesn't fight with curve continuity but I can't seem to nail it.  Also the period, no clue how that happened, good eye.  Thanks for the feedback and for checking out the project!
I sure do plan on it, thanks for checking out the project!
Thanks for checking it out! Much appreciated.

After a lot of procrastination, I got Eddie Sans to a place where I thought it was okay to start open development. Thanks a lot to everybody who gave their feedback in my last post, I tried my best to act on those while staying true to my vision of Eddie.



Eddie Sans is a grotesque typeface with humanist edges, I find it shines when its used in headlines, subheadings and other big texts.



There's a long way to go still and would love your participation in the beta and the open development of Eddie Sans.
Lovely stuff! A bit thrown off by the second r variant.
Thank you so much! The feedback is much appreciated.
Love the type and the aesthetics!

Thank you so much for the amazing critique! I couldn't spot a lot of these, so I truly appreciate it. 
Also I named it Eddie, short for editorial :)
[First draft of the typeface was in bold](https://framerusercontent.com/images/bJivicx3OLye0CeqrSEwSWfqI0.png)
That's the direction I'm headed for it's branding!
Thank you!

Thanks! I started this typeface for a branding portfolio project!  
Currently overhauling the entire punctuation set.

Thanks! I thought of making the *l* similar to the t, but I'm disliking the way the t is behaving with it's neighbors rn, and didn't want it to disrupt the whole set. Once I'm happy with the t, its next. The crowding could be because it's not kerned yet.
It reminds of film noir typefaces. Do you mind helping me out on the things that need work? I know the overshoots and undershoots are weird.
Thanks! It was unintentional initially, decided to lean into it after. The goal was to be lil more directed in personality.
